competencies.text: Report how Louis Pasteur combined chemistry and biology to understand disease and prevent infection.

days.title: Louis Pasteur and Germ Theory
days.content:
🎯 Learning Target

By the end of today's lesson, you will be able to describe how Louis Pasteur combined chemistry and biology to develop germ theory, create pasteurization, and lay the foundation for vaccines that prevent infectious diseases.

🧑‍🔬 Who Was Louis Pasteur?

Louis Pasteur (1822–1895) was a French chemist and microbiologist whose work bridged chemistry and biology. He is considered one of the founders of microbiology and the father of modern medicine.

🔬 Major Contributions

DiscoveryWhat It DidImpact Today
Germ Theory of DiseaseProved microorganisms cause disease (not 'bad air' or spontaneous generation)Foundation of sanitation, hygiene, and disease prevention
PasteurizationHeating liquids (milk, wine, juice) to kill harmful bacteriaSafer milk, juice, and beer worldwide
Rabies VaccineDeveloped first vaccine for rabies using weakened virusRabies is now preventable with post-exposure vaccination
Anthrax VaccineCreated vaccine for livestock anthraxProtects animals and prevents human exposure
Fermentation StudiesShowed yeast (living organisms) cause fermentation, not chemical decayModern food and beverage industry

🧫 Germ Theory — The Big Idea

Before Pasteur, many scientists believed diseases arose spontaneously from non-living matter (spontaneous generation). Pasteur proved the opposite through his famous swan-neck flask experiment:

  • He boiled broth in a flask with a curved neck that let air in but trapped dust and microorganisms.
  • The broth stayed clear — no growth.
  • When he broke the neck or tilted the flask so broth touched the trapped dust, microorganisms grew.

Conclusion: Microorganisms come from existing microorganisms, not from nothing. This became the foundation of germ theory.

🥛 Pasteurization — A Practical Application

Pasteurization is the process of heating a liquid to a specific temperature for a specific time to kill harmful bacteria without destroying the liquid's flavor or nutritional value.

MethodTemperature & TimeUsed For
Low-Temp, Long-Time (LTLT)63°C for 30 minutesBatch milk processing
High-Temp, Short-Time (HTST)72°C for 15 secondsCommercial milk production
Ultra-High-Temp (UHT)135°C for 2 secondsShelf-stable milk

💉 Vaccines — Preventing Infection

Pasteur's idea: expose the body to a weakened or killed version of a pathogen so the immune system can learn to fight it.

  1. Weakened pathogen is introduced → body produces antibodies.
  2. Immune system 'remembers' the pathogen.
  3. If the real pathogen attacks later → body fights it off quickly.

This principle is the basis of every modern vaccine, from polio to COVID-19.

🌍 Real-Life Legacy

  • Safe milk: Every carton of fresh milk you drink is pasteurized.
  • Hospital hygiene: Handwashing, sterilization, and disinfection come from germ theory.
  • Vaccination programs: DepEd requires immunization records for enrollment — a direct result of Pasteur's work.
  • Food safety: FDA Philippines enforces pasteurization standards.

📌 Quick Check

  • What did Pasteur's swan-neck experiment disprove? (Answer: spontaneous generation)
  • What is pasteurization? (Answer: heating liquids to kill harmful bacteria)
  • How do vaccines work? (Answer: expose the body to weakened pathogens to build immunity)

days.title: Match Game — Pasteur's Contributions
days.content:
🔗 Activity 1 — Match the Pairs

Match each of Pasteur's contributions or concepts to its correct description. There are 8 pairs and unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

match.right: Microorganisms cause disease — not spontaneous generation
Disproved spontaneous generation using boiled broth
Heating liquids to kill harmful bacteria
First vaccine for a human viral disease
Developed for livestock, protecting both animals and humans
Process where yeast produces alcohol and CO₂ in the absence of oxygen
High-Temperature Short-Time pasteurization at 72°C for 15 seconds
Body's ability to fight off a pathogen it has previously encountered

days.title: Scenario Challenge — Chemistry Meets Biology
days.content:
🎯 Activity 2 — Scenario Challenge

Read each scenario and choose the best reasoning. There are 5 scenarios. You have unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

scenario.text: 🥛 A small sari-sari store owner notices that fresh carabao milk spoils after 2 days, but the pasteurized milk in cartons lasts a week. What explains this difference?

choices.label: A) Pasteurized milk has more sugar.
B) Pasteurization kills most harmful bacteria, so spoilage takes longer.
D) Carton milk contains no water.

scenario.text: 💉 A child receives a polio vaccine. What does the vaccine contain?

choices.label: A) A strong dose of live polio virus
B) A weakened or inactivated form of the polio virus

scenario.text: 🧪 Pasteur's swan-neck flask experiment showed that when broth was exposed to dust, microorganisms grew. What did this prove?

choices.label: A) Life arises spontaneously from broth
B) Microorganisms come from pre-existing microorganisms in the air, not from nothing
C) Broth is immune to microorganisms
D) The flask's shape creates life

scenario.text: 🏥 A nurse washes hands before handling a patient. Which of Pasteur's discoveries does this practice come from?

choices.label: B) Germ theory — microorganisms cause disease

scenario.text: 🍷 A winemaker adds yeast to grape juice to produce wine. Pasteur proved that this process is caused by what?

choices.label: A) Spontaneous chemical reactions with no biological cause

days.title: Formative Check — Escape the Pasteur Lab
days.content:
🔐 Formative Check — Escape the Pasteur Lab

You have 3 lives and 6 keys to unlock. You need 75% (5 of 6) to pass. Take your time — read every option carefully.

escape.text: What is Louis Pasteur best known for?

choices.label: B) Developing germ theory and pasteurization
B) Heats liquids to kill harmful bacteria without ruining the flavor
C) Freezes food to kill bacteria
D) Removes all water from milk

escape.text: The swan-neck flask experiment disproved which theory?
Which vaccine did Pasteur develop first for a human disease?
In Pasteur's time, many doctors did not wash their hands between patients. Which of his discoveries would have prevented many deaths if applied?

choices.label: A) Killing all bacteria in the body
B) Training the immune system with weakened or inactive pathogens
